This command allows you to zip files of any kind. To use it, use this example:

To zip a text file use: zip dummy.zip dummy.txt 

Please note that each file name is a just a reference on the order the file names must go in the terminal.
This command lists the current directory content in its current location, unless a path is specified in the command.

The nano command opens a lightweight, beginner-friendly text editor directly inside your terminal window. It allows you to quickly create, view, or modify code and configuration files without launching a separate graphical application.

The rm -f command forcefully and permanently deletes files without asking for confirmation or sending them to the Trash. The **`-f`** (force) flag bypasses read-only warnings and silences error messages if the targeted file does not exist.
